reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short at around 5 feet 2 inches is a well-known historical misconception. At his autopsy, Napoleon was recorded as measuring 5 feet 2 inches in pre-metric French units (*pieds de roi* and *pouces*). When converted to modern/British imperial units, this equates to roughly 5 feet 6 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (approximately 168–170 cm). During the early 19th century, the average height for an adult French male was between 5 feet 2 inches and 5 feet 6 inches, meaning Napoleon was of average or slightly above-average height for his time, rather than unusually short. The myth of his diminutive stature was further popularized by contemporary British propaganda and political caricatures (such as those by James Gillray).
